title: Derived extension-by-zero base change
statement:
Let $\square$ be an
open-immersion square and let
$\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. For every
$K\in D^+(U_{\Et},\Lambda)$ the map of
[lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change] is an isomorphism

$$
g^{-1}j_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j'_!g_U^{-1}K
$$

in $D^+(X'_{\Et},\Lambda)$, and the isomorphism is natural in $K$,
is the identity for $g=\operatorname{id}$, and is compatible with
pasting of open-immersion squares.

proof.text: Work throughout with sheaves of modules over the constant finite ring $\Lambda$ on the small etale sites. The square gives open immersions $j,j'$ and arbitrary scheme morphisms $g,g_U$. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] the two inverse images are additive and exact on these module categories, and by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] the two extensions by zero are additive and exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to each of the four functors: their termwise complex functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms and induce functors on $D$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], $H^r(F_DK)\cong F(H^rK)$, so each preserves the lower cohomological bound of $K$ and restricts to $D^+$. Thus the two composite functors in the statement have exactly the stated source and target; no resolution or flatness assumption on a scheme morphism is required.

Write $b_{g,F}:g^{-1}j_!F\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!g_U^{-1}F$ for the degreewise map of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change]. The underived compatibility statement [lem-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change-underived-compatibility] identifies $b$ with the inverse of the module base-change mate $\beta$, gives its adjunction transpose, and normalizes its restriction to the open as the identity. This identifies the actual canonical module map used below, not merely an unspecified isomorphism.

The module theorem [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules] says that $\beta$ and its inverse are natural in the module sheaf. By [lem-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change-underived-compatibility], $b=\beta^{-1}$. Explicitly, for $t:F\to F'$, the naturality equation for $\beta$ is $\beta_{F'}\circ j'_!g_U^{-1}(t)=g^{-1}j_!(t)\circ\beta_F$. Multiplication on the left by $b_{g,F'}$ and on the right by $b_{g,F}$ gives $b_{g,F'}\circ g^{-1}j_!(t)=j'_!g_U^{-1}(t)\circ b_{g,F}$. This is the equation needed for the differentials of a complex.

For the identity square ($g=\mathrm{id}_X$, $g_U=\mathrm{id}_U$, $j'=j$), the explicit transpose in [lem-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change-underived-compatibility] says that $b_{\mathrm{id},F}^{-1}$ is the transpose of $s_{\mathrm{id}}\circ\mathrm{id}_U^{-1}(\eta_{j,F})$. Here $s_{\mathrm{id}}=c_{\mathrm{id}_X,j}^{-1}\circ c_{j,\mathrm{id}_U}$ is built from the module-linear composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear], whose underlying abelian maps are those of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition]; by the unit laws in clause (1) of the latter, $c_{j,\mathrm{id}_U}=e_Uj^{-1}$ and $c_{\mathrm{id}_X,j}=j^{-1}e_X$, so after the identity comparisons $e$ the map $s_{\mathrm{id}}$ is the identity and the transpose of $b_{\mathrm{id},F}^{-1}$ is the unit $\eta_{j,F}$ of $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$, which is also the transpose of the identity. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] gives $b_{\mathrm{id},F}=\mathrm{id}$ after these identifications.

For two successive arbitrary base changes, [lem-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change-vertical-pasting] states that the composite of the two underived canonical maps equals the canonical map for the composite base change after the inverse-image composition identifications. This is exactly the vertical pasting equation needed before localization.

For composable open immersions, [lem-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change-open-pasting] gives the displayed equation relating the two successive underived maps to the map for the composite immersion, with the canonical extension-by-zero composition comparisons. The comparisons and their endpoint identifications are the ones supplied by [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition], so this proves the second pasting direction.

For a cochain complex $K^\bullet$, set $B_K^r=b_{g,K^r}$. Step 3 applied to $d^r:K^r\to K^{r+1}$ gives
$$j'_!g_U^{-1}(d^r)\circ B_K^r=B_K^{r+1}\circ g^{-1}j_!(d^r).$$
Thus $B_K$ is a chain map, and its degreewise inverse is a chain map by the same equality multiplied by the inverses. The two composites are the identity in every degree, so $B_K$ is an isomorphism of complexes, natural in chain maps. Compose this natural isomorphism with the localization functor on the target. Step 1 says both composite complex functors invert quasi-isomorphisms. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] now descends $B$ to a natural isomorphism of the induced functors on derived categories. Write $\varphi_{F,K}:F_D(QK)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(C(F)K)$ for the factorization maps of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. For two composable exact functors $F,G$, the actual comparison for their induced composite at $QK$ is
$$\psi_{G,F,K}=\varphi_{G,C(F)K}\circ G_D(\varphi_{F,K}):G_DF_D(QK)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(C(G)C(F)K).$$
It is natural in $K$ by naturality of the two $\varphi$ maps. These are precisely the $\phi_1,\phi_2$ required by clause (2) of the localization node for the two composites in this square. Therefore its formula gives the descended exchange component $\psi_{j'_!,g_U^{-1},K}^{-1}\circ Q(B_K)\circ\psi_{g^{-1},j_!,K}$. For three functors, both parenthesizations of $\psi$ expand to $\varphi_{H,C(G)C(F)K}\circ H_D(\varphi_{G,C(F)K})\circ H_DG_D(\varphi_{F,K})$; hence their coherence follows from functoriality, and equality on all $QK$ is detected by clause (3) of the localization node. Restrict to the full subcategory $D^+$, which both sides preserve by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below]. At an object represented by $K^\bullet$ the component is the class of $B_K$ after these identifications. It is therefore exactly the derived map of the underived base-change map, and is an isomorphism for every $K\in D^+(U_{\Et},\Lambda)$.

proof.text: Apply Step 4 in every degree of a representing complex for the identity square: its termwise exchange is the identity after the inverse-image identity comparisons. Apply Step 5 in every degree for successive base changes, and Step 6 for composable open immersions, including the comparison maps $c,c'$. Localization preserves the resulting identities and compositions. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] descends the endpoint comparisons and each exchange, using the $\psi$ identifications written in Step 7; it respects composition. Clause (3) detects equality of the resulting natural transformations from equality on every $QK^\bullet$. Thus all three sheaf-level equations give the corresponding derived equations. Restricting to $D^+$ proves the identity and both pasting clauses; naturality for every derived morphism was obtained by descent in Step 7.

split_report.blueprint: The original blueprint proof paragraph is realized by Step 1 (exactness), Steps 2–3 (specified underived comparison and naturality), Steps 4–6 (identity and both pasting directions), and Steps 7–8 (the original degreewise complex/localization descent). Step 3's naturality arrows are now correctly typed (from naturality of β, with b=β^{-1}). Steps 1, 7 and 8 match the exactness, bounded-below, factorization and localization clauses (2) and (3) they cite.
